political.title: Brazil presidential runoff
political.status: First round (Oct 4): Flávio Bolsonaro 47.0%, Lula 45.2%. On Oct 5 the Ibovespa jumped 8.7% to a record, the real gained ~4% and EWZ rose ~12.6% as markets priced tighter fiscal policy and rate cuts.

bullish: Credible fiscal rules and spending restraint — lowers Brazil's risk premium and long-term rates (DI futures fell ~1pt on Oct 5)
Selic rate cuts (Copom: Nov 4, Dec 9) — helps banks, retailers and other rate-sensitive stocks
Market-based Petrobras policy: fuel prices near import parity, steady dividends (Petrobras is a top EWZ holding)
Privatisations and infrastructure concessions
Negotiated relief from the 25% US Section 301 tariff on many Brazilian goods
A stronger real — boosts dollar returns on EWZ
bearish: Expansionary spending or loosening the fiscal framework — pushes rates up and the real down (the late-2022 sell-off followed spending worries)
Government intervention in Petrobras pricing, dividends or investment plans
A disputed result or institutional conflict after the runoff
Escalating trade tensions with the US
Reversal of the first-round 'election trade' if the runoff goes the other way
Non-political: weaker China demand / iron ore prices (Vale is a top EWZ holding)

A pause or a turn back to cuts would favour the beaten-down EM markets.

themes.title: Emerging-market turnaround: Turkey, Indonesia, South Africa
themes.summary: These markets have lagged on weak currencies, high rates and expensive oil. What typically turns them is some combination of falling inflation, rate cuts, a weaker US dollar and cheaper oil. Turkey has the most visible near-term trigger (inflation below 30%, possible cut Oct 22); Indonesia needs its currency to stabilise first; South Africa hinges on a calm Nov 4 election.
